If you are spending the money, of course it’s all about the price. Obviously. 
After all, unless you are a time waster, why would you go to a dealership if you knew right from the start you can’t afford even the cheapest car on their lot? 
And ten grand remain ten grand no matter how much you talk finance. So if a down payment of ten grand means 10% of the out of the door price, it means the remaining 90% have to come from somewhere, right? 
Which means going for a 50k vehicle will practically always be the better option. 
And, dear car salespeople, you can only fool people so many times before they realise they have been sold a pup. If something is an optional package, I, the buyer, can opt out of it. That’s why it’s optional. And if it’s not optional, well, it ought to be on the price tag then. Such shady tactics are something that makes you feel like not wanting to go back there as does taking out long term loans that even after three years of paying them off leave you with negative equity. I’m a little ashamed to admit this but my car was repossessed.  
I needed a reliable car for my wife and 2 kids.  
So I ended up getting a used 2019 Subaru Forester with 87k miles.  I can’t quite remember exactly the price but I think it was like 24k?  
Well my payments were $438 a month. And 3 weeks after I got it, it had issues with the struts. 
Then a cascade of issues with other things until the AC pulley seized up and it wasn’t drivable.  
I don’t make a lot of money and most of it goes to just paying bills. I couldn’t afford all those extra issues.  
Oh and I paid the extra money for whatever warranty package they had that would “fix” problems if they happen. Of course my problems didn’t count.
